patch.value: Two residual admission gaps from the PR #1772 review: an inactive duplicate inline field can take over a built-in option, and a negated mutation flag passes harness output-control admission

Raised by the fifth Codex pass on PR #1772 (2026-11-23), not reproduced here; filed instead of extending a review loop that had already converged on the reported classes. (1) Settings writer: when inline settings hold two definitions for one key, the runtime registry uses the last one. A mutateWorkspaceSettings proposal that removes the winning definition activates the earlier one, and if that one shadows a built-in option (for example a flag full on list) the admission exempts it, because assertChangedSchemaFieldsAvailable (src/sdk/extension-command-context.ts) grandfathers any definition equal to some stored entry. Compare each proposed definition with the previously effective definition for its key, so only an unchanged active definition is grandfathered. (2) Harness: when an extension augments comments with a boolean --stdin declaration, runRegisteredCommandForTest accepts options { 'no-stdin': false, outputLimit: '1' } and runs the handler with stdin true, because the admission fold (foldOptionSpellings in src/sdk/testing.ts) keeps the negated key as noStdin while the normalizer applies the negation; native --stdin --output-limit 1 is refused with read_output_mutation_conflict. Apply the declared negation rules before deciding whether the invocation mutates. Duplicate check: searched duplicate inline field definition effective key admission negated mutation flag harness; pm-3s4jwl and pm-gh1769 (closed by PR #1772) own the main fixes.

A proposal that removes the winning duplicate inline definition is judged against the definition that becomes effective, with a spec seeding two definitions for one key; The harness refuses a negated spelling of a declared mutation flag combined with output controls exactly as native dispatch does, with a parity spec
Neither a duplicate inline definition nor a negated mutation spelling escapes the admission the native paths apply
